primary.title: Benjamin Netanyahu returns as Israel’s prime minister
primary.description_short: Israel’s 37th government, led by Benjamin Netanyahu, was sworn in on December 29, 2022.
primary.description_medium: The Knesset records that Israel’s 37th government was sworn in on December 29, 2022, with Benjamin Netanyahu presenting its policy guidelines. Reuters reported his return at the head of a hard-right cabinet. The frozen record’s 2009 date is wrong for this return. The claimed Trump or Kushner connection remains unverified.
primary.description_long: This internal draft narrows the event to Benjamin Netanyahu’s return as Israel’s prime minister. The frozen record dates that return to March 31, 2009, but the supplied reporting and official Knesset record identify the relevant government formation as December 29, 2022. The Knesset says the 37th Government was sworn in that day, Netanyahu presented its policy guidelines, and the confidence vote passed 63 to 54. Reuters described his return at the head of a hard-right cabinet that promised to expand settlements in the occupied West Bank. Those sources support the corrected date and government-formation facts. They do not show that Donald Trump caused, directed, or participated in the 2022 event. The frozen record’s description of Netanyahu as Jared Kushner’s family friend has no supporting citation in the supplied packet and is not established by the Knesset release or the Reuters report used here. Keep that relationship and the entry’s relevance to a Trump-focused collection unresolved. This draft preserves a possible contextual entry for editorial review; it is not publication eligible until its Trump nexus and category are established.

source_fact_map.fact: Israel’s 37th Government, led by Benjamin Netanyahu, was sworn in on December 29, 2022.
source_fact_map.quote: The 37th Government of the State of Israel was sworn in Thursday during a festive sitting of the Knesset Plenum
source_fact_map.source_excerpt: December 29, 2022. The 37th Government of the State of Israel was sworn in Thursday during a festive sitting of the Knesset Plenum, which was held in the presence of President of the State Isaac Herzog and Supreme Court President Justice Esther Hayut. In the plenary sitting, the Government's policy guidelines were presented by the head of the new Government, MK Benjamin Netanyahu (Likud), along with the composition of the Government and the distribution of ministerial portfolios.

source_fact_map.source_excerpt: JERUSALEM, Dec 29 (Reuters) - Benjamin Netanyahu was sworn in as Israel's prime minister on Thursday in a comeback at the head of a hard-right cabinet that promises to expand Jewish settlements in the occupied West Bank and pursue other policies criticised at home and abroad.

frozen_original.title: Cambridge Analytica Harvests 87 Million Facebook Profiles for Trump Campaign
frozen_original.synopsis: Cambridge Analytica, a data firm with ties to Trump donor Robert Mercer and Steve Bannon, harvested personal data from approximately 87 million Facebook profiles without users' consent to build psychographic profiles for targeted political advertising. The firm worked directly with the Trump campaign to identify persuadable voters in swing states and deliver tailored messaging. Cambridge Analytica's CEO Alexander Nix was caught on hidden camera boasting about the firm's ability to manipulate voters and claiming the firm ran all of Trump's digital campaign. The scandal led to massive congressional hearings and a $5 billion FTC fine against Facebook.

frozen_original.title: Trump Ends Free COVID Vaccines and Testing — Reverts to 'Every Man for Himself'
frozen_original.synopsis: On January 20, 2025, the Trump administration ended all federal programs providing free COVID-19 vaccines and testing to uninsured and underinsured Americans, dismantling the infrastructure established during the pandemic. Free vaccine distribution sites, including federally funded pharmacies and community health programs, were shut down. Federal COVID test stockpiles were allowed to expire without distribution. Trump simultaneously removed all COVID-19 mitigation guidance from CDC websites. Public health experts warned the changes would disproportionately harm elderly, immunocompromised, and low-income Americans without the means to pay for private COVID care. The decision left the United States with no federal mechanism to respond to future COVID variants or surges, effectively guaranteeing that any future waves would be handled entirely at the individual level.

primary.title: Federal COVID Vaccine and Test Access Had Separate Timelines
primary.description_short: The vaccine-access program ended in August 2024; federal COVID test ordering continued into 2025.
primary.description_medium: The CDC says its Bridge Access Program for uninsured and underinsured adults ended in August 2024 after updated vaccines replaced the prior doses. Reuters reported that the Trump administration reversed a planned shutdown of COVIDtests.gov in February 2025. CNN reported that the site was not accepting new orders on March 10, while noting that a permanent shutdown was unclear. These records do not support one January 20 action ending all free vaccines and tests.
primary.description_long: CDC records show that the Bridge Access Program provided free COVID-19 vaccines to adults without insurance or whose plans did not cover the full cost. After the FDA authorized updated 2024–25 vaccines on August 22, 2024, the earlier doses could no longer be administered and CDC said the program had ended. That was before the second Trump administration. The federal at-home test program followed a different timeline: Reuters reported that the administration reversed a planned February 2025 shutdown of COVIDtests.gov, which shipped free tests to households. On March 10, CNN reported the site was not accepting new orders, but said it was unclear whether the program had shut down permanently. These separate records do not support the frozen entry’s assertion that one January 20 decision ended all free vaccine and test programs. The accessed sources also do not establish that all CDC mitigation guidance was removed, that federal test stockpiles were allowed to expire, or that the country had no federal response mechanism. Those claims are excluded pending specific evidence.

frozen_original.title: Trump bans encrypted messaging apps for federal employees over spying concerns
frozen_original.synopsis: The Trump administration banned federal employees from using encrypted messaging applications, effectively requiring communications to remain accessible to government surveillance and monitoring. The ban targeted apps like Signal, WhatsApp, and others that provide end-to-end encryption, forcing government employees to use less secure communication channels. Cybersecurity experts warned the ban actually made government communications more vulnerable to foreign intelligence services, while the administration's real motivation appeared to be monitoring internal dissent among federal workers.

primary.original_title: Trump bans encrypted messaging apps for federal employees over spying concerns

source_fact_map.fact: Reuters reported on the Trump administration’s use of Signal, contradicting the frozen record’s categorical assertion that the administration banned employees from using encrypted messaging apps.
source_fact_map.quote: The Trump administration sought to put the scandal over its use of the Signal messaging app behind it on Monday
source_fact_map.source_excerpt: WASHINGTON, March 31 (Reuters) - The Trump administration sought to put the scandal over its use of the Signal messaging app behind it on Monday, calling it case closed, even as the breach provoked bipartisan criticism and opened up divisions inside the White House.

source_fact_map.fact: NARA says federal employees may conduct official business on third-party messaging apps subject to federal recordkeeping rules.
source_fact_map.quote: Officers or employees of federal agencies may conduct official business using third-party messaging apps.
source_fact_map.source_excerpt: Officers or employees of federal agencies may conduct official business using third-party messaging apps. However, the FRA imposes strict requirements on the use of personal accounts to conduct agency business. If any agency employee uses a personal account to engage in official business, they must: (1) copy their official account when creating or sending the message, or (2) forward a complete copy of the record to an official account within 20 days. 44 U.S.C. § 2911.
